title: Instrumentation workshop retro and metrics sprint notes
content:
Context and purpose:
This doc captures notes, decisions, and follow-ups from the 2-day instrumentation workshop (Jan 29–30, 2025) and the subsequent metrics sprint kickoff. Goal was to reduce investigation time for token-serving regressions, create a compact dashboard template for oncall, and define a small set of metric & trace contracts teams can adopt quickly.

High-level outcomes (TL;DR):
- Agreed on a minimal metric surface for token-serving: request_count, tokens_generated, p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end and model-only), kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size_distribution, and error_rate_by_phase.
- Lightweight trace span naming convention proposed (see section below).
- Canaries + synthetic probes will target 95th percentile latency and cold-cache flows.
- Dashboard wireframes: compact incident view (top), heatmap latency by route (middle), KV cache heatmap and cohort warmth (bottom).

Workshop notes (raw):
- Day 1: inventory and whiteboarding. Lots of shorthand on the board; captured three main investigation scenarios: token-surge (traffic spike), cold-cache per-tenant / route, and model fallbacks.
- Day 2: hands-on proto: instrumented 3 endpoints in the sandbox with the new metric names. Traces sampled at 10% for normal flow, 100% for errors and canary traffic.
- Quick Wins identified: prefix cache hit metric (per-tenant), batch size histogram, and a small set of error labels to indicate phase (parse/prompt-compile/runtime/postprocess).
- Friction: retro noted we should minimize cardinality for the oncall dashboard. Avoid tagging at free-form prompt level.

Proposed metric definitions (minimal contract):
- request_count: counter (unit: requests), tag by route, model_name, deployment_zone. Use delta over 1m/5m windows.
- tokens_generated: counter (unit: tokens). Tag by route, model_name, tenant_id. Include breakdown for prompt vs generated (prompt_tokens, gen_tokens).
- latency_ms: histogram + derived quantiles. Record end_to_end_latency_ms and model_infer_latency_ms. Buckets: [1,5,10,25,50,100,200,500,1000,2500]. Quantiles of interest: p50/p95/p99.
- kv_cache_hit_rate: gauge (0..1) computed as kv_hits / kv_lookups over 1m windows. Tags: route, tenant.
- batch_size_distribution: histogram of batch sizes used in runtime. Buckets: [1,2,4,8,16,32,64].
- error_rate_by_phase: counter with label phase={ingest,compile,model,postproc}. Separate 4xx vs 5xx semantics.
- synthetic_probe_success: gauge (0 or 1) per probe id. Used for canary SLOs.

Metric naming and tag guidance (to prevent explosion):
- Metric names must be snake_case, descriptive; tags are limited to route/model/zone/tenant where necessary.
- Avoid adding prompt hashes, user_ids, or free-form tags. If needed, create pre-aggregated cohort labels (e.g., tenant_tier=free|pro|enterprise).

Tracing conventions (proposal):
- Trace root: request span (name: request.<route-name>). Attributes: request_id, route, model_name, tenant_id (if available), start_time.
- Child spans:
  - parse_input (timing: prompt parsing + validation)
  - prompt_compile (feature: prompt templating + tool calls)
  - routing_decision (includes routing_reason: cost|latency|policy)
  - batch_wait (time waiting to be batched)
  - model_infer.kv_fetch (KV cache lookup; include kv_hit boolean attr)
  - model_infer.decode (actual token generation time)
  - postprocess (including safety checks, formatting)
- Error handling: spans that fail should set span.status=ERROR and include error.phase and error.code attributes.
- Sampling: default probabilistic sampling 5–10% for normal traffic (adjustable); always sample requests that exceed p95 latency, and all errors. Canaries and scheduled probes are always sampled.

Dashboard sketch (operators compact view):
Top row (incident triage):
- Live synthetic probe status (small tiles per region)
- Top 5 routes by recent p95 latency increase (sparkline + delta)
- Error rate heatmap by phase (small stacked bars)
Middle row (detail):
- Latency heatmap by route X hour (color=quantile deviation)
- Model vs end-to-end latency stacked waterfall (exploded bars show parse/compile/batch/wait/model/postproc)
- Batch size histogram over 1h/24h windows
Bottom row (cache & cost):
- KV cache hit rate by tenant cohort (trend lines)
- Tokens per second and token cost estimate (back-of-envelope)
- Recent traces quicklinks (sampled traces with annotations)

Oncall playbook snippets (for inclusion in incident runbooks):
- If p95 spikes and synthetic_probes_green=true: investigate model_infer_latency_ms and batch_size_distribution (possible batch thrash).
- If kv_cache_hit_rate drops sharply: check cache eviction logs and per-tenant cold starts; warm key counts and rehydrate policy metrics.
- If errors concentrated in postproc: look at safety filter releases / new regex rules (check PRs for last 24h).

Sprint action items (owners + rough ETA):
- API: add model_infer_latency_ms histogram + batch_size histogram to existing exporter (owner: Diego Ramos, ETA: 2025-03-14) -> JIRA-OBS-4230
- Runtime: emit kv_cache_hit and kv_lookup counters with tenant tag (owner: Lina Xu, ETA: 2025-03-21) -> JIRA-OBS-4237
- Dashboards: create "operators compact view" template and wire to sample datasets (owner: Samir Kulkarni, ETA: 2025-03-18) -> PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/238
- Tracing: implement span naming helpers and adaptive sampling rules (owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2025-03-10) -> JIRA-OBS-4241
- Docs: produce short guide "How to instrument a route" with examples and minimal tags (owner: Asha Patel, ETA: 2025-03-04) -> Confluence OBS-INSTR-2025

Open questions (for architecture review):
- Tenant tagging: do we accept tenant_id as tag for metrics, or only cohort (tier) to avoid cardinality? (security/privacy implications too).
- KV cache visibility: should we capture per-key stats for debugging (high cardinality) and if so, how to sample/aggregate?
- Batch visibility: do we export a unique batch id for each model_infer span to join traces with batch metrics? performance cost?

Notes to self / workshop retro bullets:
- Keep onboarding docs super short (<2 pages) with copy-paste examples. Folks drop this if they need to write a lot of boilerplate.
- We accidentally instrumented a debug metric with tenant_id free-form; flagged and removed in the sandbox. Reminder to run cardinality-checker before merge.
- Good energy from SREs and runtime team; cross-team pairing was invaluable. Schedule follow-up "instrumentation pairing hour" every Wednesday for the next 6 weeks.

Appendix: quick example instrument code (pseudo):
- counter.increment("tokens_generated", {route: route, model: model_name}, token_count)
- histogram.observe("model_infer_latency_ms", model_duration_ms, {model: model_name})
- gauge.set("kv_cache_hit_rate", hits/lookups, {tenant_cohort: tier})

References and links:
- Confluence draft: OBS-INSTR-2025 (linked above)
- Jira epic: JIRA-OBS-4192 (workshop epic)
- Example PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/238

- [ ] Lina: prototype kv eviction counters and sample exporter (ETA 2025-03-21)
